newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara Malaysia says staff cuts soon.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara Malaysia says staff cuts soon.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank said on Thursday that the retrenchment of around a third of its staff will begin this year and is likely to be completed by next year.

"The exercise will begin in late October or early November," Bank Negara Deputy Governor Fong Weng Phak told reporters after opening a conference on human resources in the financial services industry.

Bank Negara said earlier this week that it was closing down six of its 12 branches as part of a restructuring programme, following studies that concluded the Bank should discontinue retail operations.
Bank Negara said electronic mail and other computerised processes had also eliminated the need for so many branches.

The Bank will soon call a meeting of personnel directors from all financial institutions and insurance firms in an effort to find new jobs for redundant staff, mostly junior clerical workers, security guards and support staff, Fong said.
"It is a multi-pronged comprehensive programme to help our staff relocate themselves to other institutions and environments," he added.
"Ultimately, we're talking between 600 and 800 to 900 theoretically," out of a total staff of 2,800, he said.
The retrenchment plan was a culmination of studies initiated when Bank Negara Governor Ahmad Mohamed Don took office on May 1, 1994, Fong said.
Ahmad began by asking about the Bank's mission, how it should develop, and what are the shared values among staff, Fong said.

Negara also wanted to set an example to Malaysian financial institutions, which face increasing competition in the years ahead, now that Malaysia has signed a financial services liberalisation accord under the World Trade Organisation.
"We have been preaching to commercial banks to gear up for competition," Fong said. "And if we preach too much...then we should look to our own back yard."
